newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms on BOT talk, interbank drops late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms on BOT talk, interbank drops late.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the U.S. dollar in late trade on Tuesday on talk of the possible intervention by the Bank of Thailand to ease selling pressure against the currency, dealers said.
"The baht rose sharply in late afternoon after heavy selling of the dollar. There was talk about the central bank's possible intervention, but I cannot confirm," said one dealer at a European bank.
The baht was traded at 25.925/25.935 to the dollar late against 25.940/25.945 early, dealers said.

"The downward trend of the interbank rate will continue as some money still flowed back to the system. But the fall will also depend on how there is buying of the dollar," said one money market dealer.
The baht/dollar swap premiums rose to 14.50/15.50 satangs per a dollar late from 15.00/16.00 in the morning trade.

BOT governor Rerngchai Marakanond re-emphasised on Tuesday that the central bank would use a high interest policy to curb speculators. The BOT and the finance ministry also denied a wire service report that changes may be made to the current four-satang trading range of the baht against the dollar between the central bank and comercial banks.
